title: Shout It Out
story: You and your friends are playing the whisper-shout game. One person whispers a word, and the next person has to shout it as loud as they can. Your program can do the same thing: take quiet lowercase text and transform it into LOUD CAPITALS � or the other way around!
why: Transforming text between uppercase and lowercase is one of the most common operations in programming � used everywhere from search bars to name tags to formatting titles.
analogy: `string.str_upper` and `string.str_lower` are like a volume knob for text � turn it up to SHOUT or down to whisper, and the original stays the same.
try_it: Convert your friend's name to ALL CAPS. Then try a sentence with mixed case like 'ThE qUiCk BrOwN fOx'. What happens when you apply `string.str_upper` to it? What about `string.str_lower`? Can you whisper AND THEN shout the same message?
tips: `string.str_upper` and `string.str_lower` return a NEW string � the original string is never changed.
Numbers and symbols like `123`, `!`, `?` are not letters, so they stay the same.
You can chain transformations: pass the result of one function into another if you need to.
Use uppercase for emphasis in your output � like printing a warning or a title.
common_mistakes: Expecting the original to change: `string.str_upper(message);` by itself doesn't store the result � you need `let shout = string.str_upper(message);`.
Forgetting that these functions only work on strings � passing a number will cause an error.
Calling functions on a variable that doesn't exist yet � create the variable first, then transform it.
